newsitem.title: USA: Ex-manager of Bank of Greece guilty of fraud.
newsitem.headline: Ex-manager of Bank of Greece guilty of fraud.

text.p: The former manager of the Boston branch of the National Bank of Greece on Tuesday pleaded guilty as part of an agreement in federal court to 22 charges of fraud, theft and embezzlement.

Lakis Theoharis, 44, stood with his head bowed and occasionally covered his eyes as U.S. District Judge Mark Wolf read each of the charges detailing how the former bank manager illegally diverted funds from accounts in order to buy stock in companies listed on the Athens Stock Exchange as well as on the U.S. exchanges.

In agreeing to plead guilty, Theoharis admitted he used his position as manager of the branch from 1988 until his termination in 1991 to create phony loans, overdraft customer accounts and embezzle bank funds to support various stock transactions for himself and others.

Theoharis was indicted in June along with two other former bank employees, Peter Bakeas and Alice Andrews. Assistant U.S. Attorney Victor Wild told Wolf that Theoharis had agreed to testify against his co-defendants.
Nonetheless, the judge reminded Theoharis that he could still face up to 30 years in prison and $1 million in fines for each count if he failed to life up to the plea agreement.
Theoharis was allowed to remain free on bail pending a Nov. 26 hearing.
